claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has room-temperature tensile ductility of 8–16%.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance and undergoes pesting during conventional high-temperature air exposure.
Pre-oxidation at approximately 800 °C in about 1% O₂ for 30 minutes will form an HfO₂ surface layer on equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The pre-oxidation treatment will produce an ultrathin HfO₂ layer.
The resulting HfO₂ layer will be continuous, uniform, coherent, and adherent.
The HfO₂ layer forms directly through oxidation of Hf in the alloy.
Low-oxygen pre-oxidation limits the extent of oxidation while forming a protective scale.
The HfO₂ scale acts as a diffusion barrier that reduces subsequent oxygen ingress.
The pre-oxidation treatment leaves the bulk alloy composition intact.
The pre-oxidation treatment leaves the bulk alloy microstructure intact.
Preservation of the bulk composition and microstructure avoids adverse effects on mechanical properties.
Pre-oxidized material will have lower oxidation kinetics than untreated material during subsequent high-temperature air exposure.
Pre-oxidized material will exhibit less pesting than untreated material during subsequent high-temperature air exposure.
Pre-oxidation will preserve room-temperature ductility and strength relative to untreated material.
Pre-oxidation will preserve high-temperature ductility and strength relative to untreated material.
The proposed improvement applies to air exposures up to 1000 °C for about 5 hours and mechanical testing at strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹.
Long-term adhesion and uniformity under thermal cycling or exposures beyond the stated duration are uncertain.
